name: Philip
description: Man living at the time of the New Testament

points: The saying pleased the multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost, with Philip and the others, and set them before the apostles, who prayed and laid hands on them. Men are not picked because they ask to be officers or captains; they must fit the criteria and have served for a time, with a pattern of good works, full of the Holy Ghost and full of wisdom.

note.label: Acts 6: The Grecians Were Greek-Speaking Israelites

points: Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria and preached Christ unto them. Philip was preaching to the Jews who lived in Samaria, not yet to the Gentiles; the Most High moves in order, causing interruptions and persecutions to push his chess pieces and further spread the gospel.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: “Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ unto them.” Philip preached Christ in Samaria during the persecution.

note.label: GENTILES: NORTHERN KINGDOM IN THE NEW TESTAMENT

points: But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of the Most High and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women. Then Simon himself believed also, and was baptized, and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs. Some of our brothers recover themselves, though the outside history says Simon never truly recovered and went back to what he was doing.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: You might be asking, didn't Philip preach to the Ethiopian eunuch? We just read in Acts 11 the gospel was being preached to none but the Jews only. So what's going on in Acts 8?
Philip asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? And he said, How can I, except some man should guide me? That is a profound statement.

The eunuch was returning, sitting in his chariot, reading Esaias the prophet, and the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and join thyself to this chariot. Philip ran and heard him read Isaiah and asked, Understandest thou what thou readest? The eunuch answered, How can I, except some man should guide me, and desired Philip to come up and sit with him.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: The eunuch asked Philip, Of whom speaketh the prophet this, of himself or of some other man? He did not know, so rather than assume or give his own interpretation, he asked. That is how you should handle what you do not know: write it down and ask, rather than making an assumption and teaching others, which is how heresies come into the body. Then Philip opened his mouth, began at the same scripture, and preached unto him Jesus, because Philip had the Holy Ghost, wisdom, and understanding, having learned under the feet of the apostles.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way rejoicing. But Philip was found at Azotus, and passing through he preached in all the cities till he came to Caesarea.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

points: Philip was an evangelist, meaning he traveled and taught the word of God; an evangelist is also a prophet.
